requirements: Repeated or stale job sightings must not become duplicate or misleading notifications.
Investigate alert semantics without turning on the scheduler, email or automated applications.

evidence: AC1 DELIVERED 2026-09-25: docs/ALERTS-DOMAIN.md. Central decision - an alert is a SIGHTING RECORD, not a notification. Modelled as a notification its identity would be tied to a delivery, so re-delivery would mean re-alerting; modelled as a sighting record, delivery becomes an optional projection and "did we already tell them" is answered by state on the record rather than by remembering what was sent. That is what lets AC3 hold without a placeholder delivery mechanism.

IDENTITY GROUNDED IN THE REAL SCHEMA, not invented: job_sightings is already keyed (ownerId, fingerprint) with firstSeenAt, lastSeenAt and a distinct-searches count, and already demonstrates the required pattern - a posting seen again updates lastSeenAt, it does not become a new row. The alert key extends it by savedSearchId (CS-42) DELIBERATELY: the same posting matching two different saved searches is two different pieces of information, and keyed only by (ownerId, fingerprint) the second match would be silently swallowed.

AC1 FRESHNESS FOLLOWS CS-27 IMPLEMENTATION, NOT ITS DOCS: check-lead-liveness.ts defines CheckResult = live | stale | unknown and returns unknown for a blocked dispatcher, an unresolvable host and too many redirects, reserving stale for an unambiguous 404/410. Alerts must carry that three-state vocabulary through to the owner and MUST NOT collapse unknown into stale. Two inferences are forbidden by name: an uncertain posting is not a closed posting, and an OLD posting is not a closed posting - age is not evidence. Retention may REMOVE an old alert; nothing may REINTERPRET it as closed.

AC1 RE-MATCH RULE IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO REGRESS: re-matching must not clear readAt or dismissedAt. Dismissal is about the posting, not about the sighting - resurrecting a dismissed alert because the job was seen again would make dismissal useless exactly for the postings an owner sees most often. Stated with its consequence: a discovery run returning the same 40 postings daily must produce ZERO new alerts; if it produces 40 the symptom is an owner who stops reading alerts entirely.

AC2 SPECIFIED, NOT TESTED (half met): replay, duplicate, malformed, foreign-owner and deleted-saved-search behaviours are defined, plus four testing traps. Alert-specific trap: the dedup test must run the same match TWICE and assert count is still 1 - asserting "an alert exists" after ONE match passes against an implementation with no deduplication at all. Also carried forward: pair every negative with a positive on the same surface (a foreign-owner "no alert" assertion passes trivially against a pipeline producing no alerts for anybody), and unknown must be asserted DISTINCTLY from stale or the test passes against the exact defect AC1 forbids.

AC2 DELIVERY BUDGETS SPECIFIED BEFORE ANY DELIVERY EXISTS, so they are bounded from the start rather than after the first incident: per-owner cap with overflow SUMMARISED rather than dropped ("and 12 more" is information, silence is not); retries reuse the existing outbox/idempotency contracts rather than a second delivery mechanism; an exhausted retry budget must never mark an alert read or dismissed as a side effect of a delivery problem; no unbounded fan-out (500 matches is one summarised notification, never 500).

AC3 MET: no email provider, no background delivery, no scheduling, no placeholder channel. Alerts are READ, not pushed - until a channel is approved an alert is something the owner sees when they open the application, which is a complete and useful feature on its own and needs no external approval. Any later scheduled integration must satisfy CS-26 and the existing outbox/idempotency contracts rather than introducing a parallel queue.

evidence: AC1 + AC3 DELIVERED 2026-09-25: docs/ACCOUNT-RECOVERY-THREAT-MODEL.md. Requirements and threat model only - no route, no token, no page, no email. Recovery is documented separately from the two surfaces that already exist and were verified at source: POST /api/account/password (authenticated, rate-limited password:${ownerId} 5/hour) and manual operator recovery. POST /api/register is confirmed disabled, returning 404 "Registration unavailable" - it already refuses to confirm it exists.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT DEFINES THE THREAT MODEL: authenticated password change is guarded by a secret only the owner knows; recovery is guarded by ACCESS TO A MAILBOX, so it is a second, weaker authentication path onto the same account whose security ceiling is an email account CareerScope does not control. Enabling it permanently changes what an attacker needs from "the password" to "the password OR the mailbox". That is why AC3s approval gate is substantive rather than procedural.

BLOCKER DISCOVERED WHILE WRITING, NOT VISIBLE FROM THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA - AC2 requires BOUNDED ATTEMPTS and recovery is unauthenticated, so there is no ownerId to key on. Both available keys are currently unusable. (1) IP keying is inert: /api/login and /api/register hash request.ip, and per CS-59 verified at source Caddy proxies over loopback in a shared network namespace with header_up -X-Forwarded-For DELETING the header, so request.ip is 127.0.0.1 for every production request. Those limiters are not per-client at all - they are ONE GLOBAL BUCKET shared by the entire internet, which any single client can exhaust for everyone. A recovery endpoint keyed the same way would satisfy "bounded attempts" on paper with a control that bounds nothing per attacker.

BLOCKER PART 2 - EMAIL KEYING TURNS THE LIMITER INTO AN ENUMERATION ORACLE, and the collision is easy to miss because each control is correct in isolation. If the limiter rejects with 429 while normal submission returns 202, the response distinguishes a repeatedly-submitted address from an unknown one - an enumeration oracle BUILT OUT OF THE CONTROL MEANT TO PREVENT ABUSE - and it lets an attacker deny a known victim recovery by exhausting their bucket deliberately. RESOLUTION, the load-bearing rule of the document: the limiter must gate the SIDE EFFECT, never the RESPONSE. A rate-limited recovery request returns the same 202 and the same body and simply sends nothing. A recovery endpoint that CAN return 429 has already failed AC2 regardless of how well its limits are tuned.

DEPENDENCY CS-59 ADDED TO THIS TICKET (was empty). CS-44 cannot honestly satisfy AC2 while every client shares one rate-limit key. Recording that dependency is the most useful output of this ticket - it would otherwise have been discovered mid-implementation, or not at all.

AC2 SPECIFIED, NOT TESTED: non-enumerating responses closed at four leakage sources rather than the obvious one (status/body, TIMING - an existing account does hash work a missing one does not, and an unmeasured constant-time claim is a check that cannot fail - error paths, and logs). Token requirements: hashed at rest like a password so a database disclosure yields no usable tokens; absolute non-sliding expiry; atomic single-use because a read-then-write check has a race; and expired must be INDISTINGUISHABLE from invalid or expiry becomes a probe for whether a token was ever real.

AC2 ORIGIN HANDLING - the reset link origin comes from server configuration, NEVER from the request. A Host or X-Forwarded-Host header echoed into an email body is a token-exfiltration primitive: the attacker submits the victims address, the victim receives a genuine email from the real sender, and the link points at the attacker. Plus no open redirect after reset, no token in a query string that survives into a referrer, and no third-party resources on the reset page.

AC2 SESSION INVALIDATION stated with its real verification: a completed reset must kill EVERY session for the account, not just the one performing it, because recoverys main legitimate use is suspected compromise and leaving the attackers session alive defeats the purpose. Verification is NOT "the user can log in with the new password" - it is that a session established BEFORE the reset no longer works.

AC2 FIXTURE TRAPS, carried forward and sharpened: every negative needs a positive on the same surface in the same test ("no email sent to the foreign address" passes against a build that sends nothing to anybody); the non-enumeration test must compare two responses BYTE FOR BYTE rather than assert each is 202 separately, because two 202s with different bodies both pass a per-response assertion and still leak; the single-use test must run CONCURRENTLY since a sequential double-redemption passes against the read-then-write race that is the defect worth catching; and the origin test must supply a hostile Host header and assert whose host the emitted link contains, not that it is well-formed.

STATUS HELD AT DISCOVERY: AC1 and AC3 met by the document, AC2 specified but no fixtures written, and implementation is gated on owner approval of sender, domain, secret handling and this security design PLUS closure of CS-59. Registration stays disabled and existing recovery stays available, per AC3. Until all four approval conditions hold the correct state is exactly the current one.

REVIEWER VERDICT 2026-09-25: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS, and assessed the STRONGEST OF THE THREE - "this one does not read as written under time pressure". Every code claim it makes verified FACT, including header_up -X-Forwarded-For in BOTH Caddyfile blocks plus trustProxy: false. All findings fixed in the document. Ticket correctly remains DISCOVERY.

F-3 FIXED - A GENUINE GAP THE DOCUMENT DID NOT NAME. It required a completed reset to invalidate every session, but said nothing about OUTSTANDING RESET TOKENS WHEN A PASSWORD CHANGES THROUGH THE AUTHENTICATED ROUTE. The sequence is the realistic one: an attacker submits the victims address so a live token exists, the victim suspects compromise and changes their password through the authenticated route, and the attackers token remains valid. The document now states that a password change through ANY route invalidates all outstanding reset tokens - a recovery token is an alternative proof of ownership, so changing the credential must retire every outstanding proof, not only the sessions. It matters because IT IS PRECISELY WHAT A COMPROMISED OWNER WILL ACTUALLY DO; they will not think to cancel a reset email they never requested.

F-1 FIXED: the CS-59 dependency WAS added to backlog.json, but the document still read as though it were outstanding and the paragraph appeared twice. Now recorded once, as a dependency already captured.

F-2 FIXED: "blocked on CS-59" read as a sequencing note. The document now says plainly that CS-59 is a PROXY-LAYER CHANGE ON A SINGLE-HOST DEPLOYMENT - the same class as the host-blocked tickets needing an operator session - and that nothing in the web or API tier can fix it, because the header is deleted before the application ever sees the request.

F-4 FIXED: the 429 fixture is now marked BLOCKED alongside the control it tests, because there is no usable rate-limit key until CS-59 is fixed and the fixture cannot be written before the limiter it asserts on exists. Marked as blocked rather than listed as merely outstanding.

F-5 FIXED: the verification-lifecycle half made the sharpest claim in the document - that an unverified account behaving differently at login IS an enumeration oracle reachable without touching recovery - and supplied no fixtures for it. A claim that sharp with nothing to falsify it is the weakest kind of assertion. Five fixtures added, with the three login responses required to be compared TO EACH OTHER byte for byte in the same test, because asserting each is a 401 separately passes while all three carry different bodies.

RECORDED AS THE POSITIVE VERDICT NOT TO BE LOST UNDER SIX FINDINGS: on the criterion that matters most - does each document name its own check-that-cannot-fail before any code exists - ALL THREE TIER C DOCUMENTS PASS. CS-44s is the sharpest, and its limiter-as-enumeration-oracle discovery converts a tuning question into a structural one: a recovery endpoint that CAN return 429 has already failed AC2, no matter how well its limits are tuned. No duplication across the three; the non-confirmation rule is consistent while correctly using DIFFERENT mechanisms for different trust contexts - 404-never-403 on authenticated surfaces, escalating to byte-identical responses and no-429 on the unauthenticated one. The escalation is principled, not accidental.

requirements: The engineering control center (scripts/engineering-ui.mjs) is deliberately loopback-only, so the owner can only see current tickets/agent state on the machine it runs on, not from a phone or a second office system.

The owner wants to check tickets from a phone or another computer. The safe, buildable half is a manually-published encrypted read-only snapshot using the pattern already built for the public admin view. Being able to add tickets remotely is a much bigger, separately-gated problem and is recorded here rather than assumed.

evidence: DESIGN DELIVERED 2026-09-29: docs/REMOTE-ENGINEERING-CONTROL-CENTER.md defines a manually published, read-only encrypted Pages snapshot reusing the existing encrypted-admin envelope, an explicit allowlist/schema version, stale-export provenance, fail-closed behavior and browser lock/refresh semantics.

SECURITY SCOPE 2026-09-29: the design excludes secrets, credentials, private profile/resume/lead data, raw findings and exploit details; it introduces no server, token, polling loop, write API or Hostinger dependency. Remote ticket creation/editing remains a separately gated design question with authentication, replay, revision, audit and sync requirements.

VERIFICATION PLAN 2026-09-29: unit, browser and Pages allowlist gates are specified with paired positive/negative fixtures; implementation is intentionally not claimed complete until those gates exist.

requirements: A user who reviews their parsed resume and explicitly declines a bad skill/title finds it silently reappearing in every future match, with no way to exclude it short of deleting the entire resume.

CS-22 wired the parsed resume into matching for the first time. Doing so activated a pre-existing, previously-dormant design characteristic: resume-derived skills and titles are unioned into every match permanently, with no way to exclude a specific one short of deleting the whole resume - which conflicts with the product's own documented 'explicit editable proposal' review step for the rest of the profile. requirements: Six systemd timers now run unattended (monitor, backup, discovery, liveness, retention, proxy-recovery). If any one of them silently stops firing - a corrupted unit, an accidental disable, a full disk preventing systemd from spawning it - nothing alerts on that absence. The backup timer failing silently is the worst case: the owner would believe recoverability exists when it does not.

Six unattended systemd timers now exist with no independent check that any of them is still actually firing. Tracked as its own ticket per the owner and ChatGPT-consulted second opinion, deliberately sequenced after the held frontend work rather than actioned immediately.

evidence: docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md - "Nothing watches the watcher" section, disclosed incrementally across CS-24/25/26/27/3

ChatGPT second opinion (owner-shared thread, 2026-09-23): acceptable as a short-term disclosed gap, but the six-timer count changes the priority; recommended one shared scheduler-health checker over six separate watchdogs, and explicit visibility to the owner in the meantime, especially for the backup timer

SIX TIMERS VERIFIED AGAINST THE REPO, not assumed: careerscope-{monitor,backup,discovery,liveness,retention,proxy-recovery} each have a .service + .timer in infra/v3. No discrepancy with the six named in the ticket. Two schedule shapes found and both handled: monitor and proxy-recovery are monotonic (OnUnitActiveSec 5min/2min); backup, discovery, liveness and retention are OnCalendar with RandomizedDelaySec 300-600s.

AC1 SATISFIED: infra/v3/scheduler-health.sh is ONE checker for all six, not six ad-hoc checks. It reads real systemd state (systemctl show: LoadState, UnitFileState, ActiveState, LastTriggerUSec, NextElapseUSec*, TimersMonotonic/Calendar, plus the triggered service Result/ActiveState/ExecMainStatus) and cross-checks systemctl list-timers. The expected interval is DERIVED FROM THE UNIT ITSELF - monotonic timers from their own OnUnitActiveUSec/OnBootUSec, calendar timers by expanding the unit own OnCalendar via systemd-analyze calendar --iterations=2 and differencing - so a schedule change in a unit file cannot silently drift from what the checker expects. It emits ONE aggregated alert reusing the existing json_escape + send_alert webhook pattern from monitor.sh/backup.sh/recover-proxy.sh (SCHEDULER_WEBHOOK_URL falling back to MONITOR_WEBHOOK_URL), https-only, edge-triggered with 6h re-notify and a one-shot recovery message.

AC3 SATISFIED AND PROVEN BEHAVIOURALLY, not just documented: grace is tiered per the ticket own HIGH/MEDIUM/LOWER ranking - backup 10% of interval (min 10m, the strictest of all six, per the ticket own reasoning that a silently dead backup is the worst case); monitor and proxy-recovery 50% (min 10m); discovery and liveness 100% (min 30m); retention 200% (min 1h). Every floor exceeds the corresponding unit RandomizedDelaySec so a randomized start is never misread as a missed run. A test asserts the ranking behaviourally: at the SAME 1.5x relative overrun, backup alerts and retention does not.

FAILURE MODES MADE STRUCTURALLY LOUD - the core of this ticket. Exit codes are deliberately NOT monitor.sh always-0 pattern: 0 = all six evaluated and healthy, 1 = a watched timer is unhealthy, 2 = STRUCTURALLY UNABLE TO VERIFY. There is no path where an unreadable state yields a healthy report. Handled as loud failures: unit not installed (LoadState != loaded); disabled or inactive; systemctl missing entirely (alert STILL sent, exit 2); systemctl erroring, empty or unparseable; LastTriggerUSec n/a, 0, epoch, absent, garbage or in the future; interval underivable (never a fallback guess); active timer with no next elapse; service Result != success; and TWO independent short-result-set assertions so fewer than six timers can never pass.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL: infra/v3/check-scheduler-health.sh runs 63 assertions, all PASS, exit 0. Valid input passes (exit 0, no alert). Invalid input fails: an overdue backup exits non-zero, the alert names exactly that timer and marks it HIGH, no other timer is named, exactly one aggregated alert is sent; a service with Result=failed exits non-zero. MALFORMED input fails loudly: LastTriggerUSec=n/a is reported as never having run rather than healthy; a missing unit exits 2 and REFUSES to call 5 of 6 a pass; systemctl returning garbage reports the parse failure once per timer; an empty read is reported, not swallowed; systemctl absent entirely still alerts rather than dying quietly. Real emitted messages were captured for the healthy, degraded, blind-missing-unit and blind-garbage cases.

THE TEST SUITE CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT IN THE CHECKER ITSELF during development: the recovery transition was logged to stdout as a plain "ok" while the word "recovered" reached only the webhook. Fixed by moving the notify decision above the log line. An earlier run also produced two failures caused by the TEST freezing "now" at suite start while the suite takes ~15 min under Git-bash - the checker was right and the fixtures were wrong; fixtures now stamp at write time. Recorded because a test that never caught anything is not evidence.

AC2 SATISFIED (documentation): docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md "Nothing watches the watcher" rewritten to PARTIALLY ADDRESSED (CS-47) with the off-host leg explicitly OPEN and NOT built - it records that a local checker dies with its VPS, detects a timer that stopped but not a host that stopped, and cannot watch its own timer. The four-stage architecture (host timers -> local scheduler-health checker -> external/off-host dead-man-switch -> alert) is recorded with stage three marked NOT BUILT. docs/OPERATIONS/MONITORING.md gained a "Scheduler health (CS-47)" runbook with the threshold table, exit codes, sanitization, the on-host stop-a-timer proof to run after installation, and install marked operator-only, not yet performed.

HIGHEST-VALUE THING TO CHECK FIRST ON THE HOST: systemctl show timestamp/timespan property rendering varies by systemd version (raw microseconds vs human string), as does systemd-analyze "Iteration #2:" vs "Iter. #2:". The parsers accept both forms and fail loudly on anything else, so the worst case is a permanent loud false alarm rather than a silent pass - the safe direction, but noisy until confirmed on Ubuntu 24.04.

requirements: CareerScope has no AI-assisted capability at all today (v2/ARCHITECTURE.md: "Inference is off... AI is DEFERRED - INTENTIONAL"). The owner wants an initial, strictly-scoped AI capability - lead-note summarization, follow-up suggestions and plain-English explanations of already-computed deterministic evidence - using only OpenRouter free (:free) models, off by default, with no paid fallback and no risk to the deterministic matching/exclusion/ranking/application engine.

First-ever AI capability for CareerScope: OpenRouter free-model-only, off by default, strictly scoped away from any deterministic decision, with real fail-fast behavior and data minimization. Implemented 2026-09-23 (preparation-coaching elaboration only, 1 of 6 originally-scoped use cases); a real design review, a real end-to-end live OpenRouter verification, a self-found-and-fixed Swagger-spec 500 bug, and a real post-implementation Security review (2 findings fixed and re-verified: wrong-directory structural test, unbounded response body) all completed before moving to QA.

evidence: Current Node 24 CI verification: runs 36385161068 and 36385785464 completed green, including the service-backed V2 integration path that exercises this provider contract.
v2/ARCHITECTURE.md:27 - "Inference is off. Ollama is not running and no external model is called... AI is DEFERRED - INTENTIONAL."
docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md:189-197 - "AI and auto-apply" - Status DEFERRED - INTENTIONAL

v2/packages/core/src/leads.ts - saved_leads.notes is the existing natural attachment point for note summarization; no schema change needed for that use case
v2/scripts/check-lead-liveness.ts - established pattern for outbound HTTP with timeout/abort handling to reuse for the OpenRouter client

FORENSIC AUDIT FINDING F-5 (P1), 2026-09-24: v2/packages/core/src/ai-provider.test.ts RAN IN NO WORKFLOW. Verified by the Orchestrator against current bytes: test:unit named exactly five files and test:integration nine, and ai-provider.test.ts was in NEITHER; only the plain "v2 npm test" glob would have found it, and no workflow invokes that. So CareerScope only outbound third-party integration had a 12-case matrix - API-key-never-logged, the oversized-response byte cap, model-catalog fail-closed, typed 401/402/429/5xx/timeout/malformed failures, and the structural test asserting matching never imports AI - and none of it ran in CI. This is the identical shape an Independent Reviewer already caught once as CS28-1, recurred undetected.

FIXED: ai-provider.test.ts added to test:unit in v2/package.json, so it runs in the existing no-services CI step. Confirmed from the test source that it is service-free and CANNOT make a real OpenRouter call - every case starts a throwaway node:http server on 127.0.0.1:0 and points the client at it via _setBaseUrlForTests; keys are literals; configuredAiProvider({}) asserts AI is disabled by default; no OPENROUTER_API_KEY is read. The CI step name and its comment were both updated, because the step deliberately says "unit only - no database, queue or browser coverage" so a green job never implies coverage it lacks, and the adjacent CS-28 comment said "test:unit five files" which this change would have turned into a lie.

PROVEN THE WIRING IS REAL, NOT MERELY PRESENT - the exact defect being fixed. test:unit before: 37 tests, 37 pass. After: 49 tests, 49 pass - an increase of exactly the 12 ai-provider cases. Orchestrator independently re-ran and confirmed 49/49 exit 0. Falsification: breaking one assertion in ai-provider.test.ts produced "not ok 19 - requestCompletion: success returns the completion text", 48 pass / 1 fail, exit 1 - proving the file is genuinely executed by that script rather than merely named. Reverted and green again.

RESIDUAL RISK, disclosed: ai-provider.test.ts is currently an UNTRACKED file. If it is not committed alongside the package.json change, CI will fail with module-not-found. That is a loud failure rather than a silent one, which is the correct direction, but it must be committed together.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (read-only, no shell). VERDICT: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS - not UAT. Architecture verified thoroughly and favourably: startup-time config validation BEFORE app.listen() so misconfiguration is a crash rather than a per-request surprise; fail-closed catalog verification; the structural test guarded by assert.ok(files.length > 10) against vacuity; the route owner-scoped, rate-limited and CSRF-enforced with a complete kind-to-status map; and a genuine throwaway node:http server per case so no real OpenRouter call is possible.

F-1 (P2, USER-VISIBLE) CONFIRMED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, with a corrected line number - the reviewer said line 53, the actual line is 56. v2/apps/web/src/components/preparation-panel.tsx renders the FIXED string "Rules-based review | AI inference off | Saved profile revision ..." directly above per-item "Get AI coaching" buttons. When AI_ENABLED=true that line is FALSE ON SCREEN, in the one UI surface AI actually reaches; when AI is off the button still renders and 503s on click. This is the same defect class as CS-51 aria-pressed: a control asserting something it does not know. FIX: derive the line from a real capability flag (GET /api/session is the natural carrier) and hide or disable the button when AI is off. NOT YET FIXED.

F-2 (P2) ACCEPTED - THE MOST IMPORTANT OF THE FOUR, because it is a check that can barely fail. The data-minimization test proving AC7 runs against a HAND-CONSTRUCTED LITERAL (evidence: [Backend Engineer]) and then asserts the request body omits email, phone, resume text and compensation - strings that were NEVER IN THE INPUT. It can therefore only fail if elaborate() itself fabricated and injected them. The one test that does build a real profile containing test@example.test never feeds it to elaborate. So AC7 ("only the minimum sanitized allowlisted fields are sent") is asserted, not proven. FIX: run prepareProfile() on a profile genuinely carrying PII, pass its real target to elaborate, and assert against the captured body - that version could actually fail. NOT YET FIXED. F-3 (INFERRED, not FACT - it did not read database.test.ts): AC10 names "owner isolation" and "provider failure isolated from the underlying operation", and NEITHER case appears in ai-provider.test.ts. Confirm whether they live elsewhere before claiming AC10. F-4: the untracked-file coupling again, which it rates the single highest-probability way CS-48 breaks main.

CS-48 F-1 FIXED 2026-09-25, and it turned out to be the SAME DEFECT as CS-39 AC2 - one fix, two tickets. The preparation screen rendered the FIXED string "Rules-based review | AI inference off | Saved profile revision N" directly above per-item "Get AI coaching" buttons. That caption is FALSE ON SCREEN whenever AI_ENABLED is true, in the one UI surface AI actually reaches; and CS-39 AC2 requires the screen distinguish its states "without implying AI", which it cannot do while simultaneously saying inference is off AND offering AI coaching. FIXED AT THE SOURCE OF TRUTH rather than by editing the string: GET /api/session now returns aiEnabled: options.aiProvider !== undefined. A screen cannot honestly describe a capability it is not told about. Only WHETHER the feature is configured is reported - never the key, the model or the provider, and that is asserted by test. The caption now reads "optional AI coaching available" when enabled and keeps "AI inference off" when not. The rules-based half never changes, deliberately: scoring, exclusions, ranking and dedup stay fully deterministic whatever the AI setting is, so the caption now says exactly that and nothing more. THE BUTTON IS GATED TOO - a control that 503s on click is the same defect in a different place. The gate lives INSIDE AiElaborate rather than at the two call sites, because one call site is in a separate Questions component with no session in scope; gating per call site would have meant threading a prop and leaving two places that could drift apart. One component owns the capability question. The typecheck caught my first attempt at this, which placed the gate at the call sites - a real error, not a style preference.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL, at the API layer, because the browser suite could not prove it: check-ui pins the AI-OFF caption and AI_ENABLED is false locally, so the enabled branch is unreachable there without flipping a production-shaped setting. Added an API-level test instead, constructing TWO apps (aiProvider is fixed at construction) with a synthetic config that reaches no network. Falsification: replacing aiEnabled with the constant false fails with "session must report aiEnabled true when a provider is configured", 42/43. Reverted, 43/43 exit 0. PER THE NEW STANDING RULE I wrote hours earlier, I verified the mutation was ACTUALLY PRESENT before running (printed the line: "L245: aiEnabled: false,") and verified the revert the same way ("L245: aiEnabled: options.aiProvider !== undefined,"). AC10 TRACED FOR A FALSE PASS AND NONE EXISTS - database.test.ts:4098-4131. EVERY FAILURE MODE IS CLOSED: a route ignoring the session and always serving owner A fails OWNER B ITERATION OF THE POSITIVE; a route returning no profile leaves bodies.length === 1 holding but fails the positive; zero provider requests fail the length guard; and two owners sharing a title makes includes(other.title) TRUE SO THE NEGATIVE FIRES LOUDLY - the degenerate fixture cannot produce a false pass, it produces a red.

AND THE COMMENT STATES THE CONSTRAINT THAT FORCED THE SHAPE: "The route takes no owner from the request - it is derived from the session - so the only way to test it is to ask the SAME checkId as two different owners and prove each got their own profile. Positive on the same surface first." THAT IS THE RULE THIS PROJECT REACHED BY WAY OF SIXTEEN FAILURES, APPLIED DELIBERATELY AT THE POINT OF WRITING, with the reasoning recorded beside it rather than discovered by a later reviewer.

RECORDED AS THE REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION FOR OWNER-ISOLATION TESTING IN THIS CODEBASE. Any future owner-scoping test should copy the shape exactly: positive on the same surface first, then the paired negative, precondition asserted, collection proven non-empty.

AND THE INSTRUCTIVE PAIR, WORTH MORE THAN EITHER TICKET ALONE: THIS TEST AND CS-33 NEGATIVE-PATH TEST LIVE IN THE SAME FILE AND ARE BOTH SOUND FOR OPPOSITE REASONS. AC10 states its precondition and non-vacuity WHERE IT IS WRITTEN and survives being split. CS-33 asserts neither, and holds only because a LATER assertion happens to prove an EARLIER one precondition - so splitting it one-test-per-behaviour would silently make half of it vacuous. PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-26: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS. The never collapse is genuinely fixed - withMockServer res is now typed ServerResponse & { req: IncomingMessage } directly, replacing Parameters<Parameters<typeof createServer>[0]>[1]. The comment diagnosis of the CAUSE is correct: createServer is overloaded, Parameters<> resolves the first overload, and its [0] is ServerOptions rather than a listener.

F-48-A - THE COMMENT MISSTATES THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS THE PART OF THE COMMENT MEANT TO PREVENT RECURRENCE. It says "every mock handler in this file was checking nothing at all - res.writeHead(...), res.anything(...), ALL EQUALLY ACCEPTED." THAT IS BACKWARDS. Property access on a never-typed value IS AN ERROR IN TYPESCRIPT, so those calls were not accepted - they would have been rejected, loudly, the moment anything type-checked the file.

VERIFIED BY MY OWN PROBE, NOT BY ACCEPTING THE REVIEW, AND IT FOUND A SHARPER FORM THAN REPORTED. Reconstructing the original alias and calling BOTH a legitimate method and a bogus one gave: TS2344 ON THE TYPE ALIAS ITSELF; TS2339 "Property writeHead does not exist on type never"; and TS2339 on the bogus method. SO EVEN THE LEGITIMATE CALL WAS REJECTED. The comment says all were equally accepted; in fact ALL WERE EQUALLY REJECTED. The polarity is exactly inverted, not merely imprecise.

AND THE PROBE CARRIED ITS OWN FALSIFICATION: a control line calling the same bogus method on a value typed any produced NO ERROR, so the probe was demonstrably capable of detecting silent acceptance. A clean result would therefore have meant something, which is what makes the dirty result evidence.

ALSO CONFIRMED FROM THE PROBE: THE TYPE ALIAS WAS ITSELF A TS2344 ERROR, so had the file ever been checked IT WOULD HAVE FAILED AT THE ALIAS - immediately and obviously - RATHER THAN SUBTLY AT THE CALL SITES. There was never a quiet-wrong state; there was only an unexamined one.

SO THE HARM WAS NEVER never. THE HARM WAS EXCLUSIVELY THAT THE FILE WAS EXCLUDED FROM TYPE-CHECKING - which is CS-76 finding, not a property of never. The distinction matters because A RECURRENCE-PREVENTION COMMENT THAT MISSTATES THE CAUSE WILL PREVENT THE WRONG RECURRENCE: someone who believes a never-typed value silently accepts any call will mis-analyse the next one. (never IS silently assignable TO anything - that part is real - but PROPERTY ACCESS ON IT IS AN ERROR, and the two are being conflated.)

FIX ROUTED TO THE v2/packages/core OWNER, NOT APPLIED HERE: amend the comment to say the expression collapsed to never AND THE FILE WAS NEVER TYPE-CHECKED, WHICH IS WHY NOBODY SAW EITHER THE COLLAPSE OR THE ERRORS IT WOULD HAVE PRODUCED. KEEP THE CLOSING LINE VERBATIM - "A test file that cannot be type-checked is the same class of problem as a test that cannot fail." That sentence is exactly right and is the one worth keeping.
F-48-A DOES NOT BLOCK UAT. The code fix is correct and independently verified; THE DEFECT IS IN THE EXPLANATION, NOT THE BEHAVIOUR. Status unchanged.

completedSteps: Rebuilt against the real owner-supplied Dashboard design image (shown directly in chat 2026-09-23, not saved to page-designs/) as a real Next.js route (/dashboard), using only real, owner-scoped API data (GET /api/profile, /api/resumes, /api/leads, /api/searches, /api/searches/:id) - every stat card, checklist item, recommended job, activity entry and skill ranking traces to a real field; no invented totals, trend deltas or profile-match percentage.

requirements.title: Identifiers are discarded between call site and destination (five instances)

requirements: Several controls do not do what they name. "Open Saved Lead" opened the Saved list but not the lead; clicking your third-most-recent search opened your most recent one. No lead was deep-linkable anywhere in the app.

Five instances of one shape: an identifier that exists at the call site is discarded before it reaches the destination. ALL FIVE ARE FIXED and verified against current bytes. Separately, F-4 (SaveJob does not hydrate already-saved state on mount) is confirmed broken, blocked on a missing backend lookup, and documented rather than faked - it is a distinct finding, not one of the five instances.

evidence: ALL FIVE CONFIRMED against current bytes before any change. saved-leads.tsx declares onOpen: (id: string) => void at line 89 and DOES supply the id (line 152 onOpen(save.data.id), line 167 same) - so the component was always correct and both consumers threw the id away: job-search-view.tsx:452 and dashboard/page.tsx:368 were each onOpen={() => router.push(/saved)}. Dropped twice over, because the destination could not have used it either: initialId was hardcoded null at saved/page.tsx:14 and applications/page.tsx:20, while SavedLeads already consumed it correctly (line 579 type, 596 useState(initialId), 593 cache read). Dashboard rendered <Link href="/jobs"> per run with no id while job-search-view.tsx:75 computed selectedId = selected ?? runs.data?.items[0]?.id from component state only, with no URL parameter anywhere in the file - so clicking any run opened the newest one. That last instance is the most serious: it silently showed the owner the wrong data.

FIXED: both onOpen call sites now pass the id through to /saved?lead=<id>. /saved and /applications read ?lead= instead of hardcoding null. job-search-view.tsx reads ?run= with the previous state-based value as fallback, and keeps the URL in sync (push when the owner picks a run so Back works, replace when the view itself created the run). Dashboard Recent Discovery links /jobs?run=<run.id>. Suspense boundaries were added following the existing app/page.tsx pattern, since useSearchParams requires one in the App Router. No route or component was removed or renamed; no styling, spacing, typography or colour was touched, per the UI freeze.

UNTRUSTED INPUT: the parameter is only ever handed to the existing owner-scoped GET /api/searches/:id and GET /api/leads/:id. Malformed gives 400, unknown or foreign-owner gives 404, both rendered by each screen existing error state. Server-side owner isolation was not touched or bypassed, and the client never treats a URL parameter as identity.

requirements.title: Security-relevant checks are enforced by no pipeline, and the glob that would have caught it is the script nobody runs

requirements: Coverage that exists but never executes is indistinguishable from no coverage, and it reads as green.

One orphaned test file, eleven unwired executable checks, a deploy gate that runs no V2 tests, and a structural cause: CI names scripts, and the glob that would catch anything unnamed is itself never invoked.

evidence: VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-25, all three claims true against current bytes. (1) NO WORKFLOW INVOKES the v2 "test" glob script: grep for "prefix v2 run test" across .github/workflows returns only test:unit (ci.yml:130), test:integration (ci.yml:265), test:backfill-job-sightings (ci.yml:273) and the newly added test:ui (ci.yml:327). CI calls scripts BY NAME. So the one script that globs every test file - and would therefore have caught ai-provider.test.ts automatically - is the script nobody runs. THAT is the generalisable lesson: naming files in scripts means a new test file is invisible by default, and the safety net exists but is unreachable.

VERIFIED: the DEPLOY GATE RUNS NO V2 TESTS. deploy.yml line 140 "npm test" sits under the step named "Test the domain packages being shipped" and is the ROOT (V1) suite; the V2 steps that follow are typecheck, lint and build only (line 146) plus a production dependency audit. Partly defensible because require-ci enforces a green CI run for the same head SHA, but the deployed application tests are covered only transitively - if that enforcement is ever bypassed or misconfigured, the deploy gate itself would not notice.

AUDIT FINDING H-1 (HIGH), accepted: the two suites that ran nowhere carry disproportionately security-relevant assertions. ai-provider.test.ts holds the API-key-never-logged assertion across 401/429/5xx/timeout/malformed, the 256 KiB bounded-read test proven with a real 400 KB payload, the model-catalog fail-closed tests, and the STRUCTURAL test asserting no sibling module in packages/core/src imports ai-provider/ai-assist - which is the mechanical enforcement of "the deterministic engine stays authoritative". check-ui.ts is the only cross-engine E2E and exercises the AUTH BOUNDARY (unauthenticated deep-link bounce, no private-content flash), the skip-link contract, and axe across ten routes.

THIS IS THE THIRD RECURRENCE OF ONE DEFECT CLASS, and the prior two are recorded in this repository own state. R3: the resume parser self-check tested for --allow-net, a Deno flag Node does not have, making the check unconditionally true while resume parsing could never have succeeded in a real deployment. CS28-1: a reviewer found backfill-job-sightings.test.ts invisible to CI. Now ai-provider.test.ts, on the one feature that sends owner content off-box. A class that recurs three times is a structural problem, not three mistakes.

STRUCTURAL HALF DONE 2026-09-25, and it was done FIRST deliberately, because fixing instances fixes files while fixing the structure fixes the class. Added v2/scripts/check-test-registration.ts plus the npm script test:registration and a CI step in the verify job. WHAT IT DOES: globs every *.test.ts under v2 (excluding node_modules, dist and .next), reads every npm script body, and treats any script naming a .test.ts path as CLAIMING that file. A file claimed by no script fails the check. It matches on the PATH rather than on script names, so a new test:whatever runner is picked up automatically - the check must not itself become the next stale enumeration, which would be the same defect one level up. WHY NOT JUST POINT CI AT THE GLOB, which is the obvious alternative and is wrong: six of these files need PostgreSQL, Redis and LocalStack. Running the glob in the no-services job would fail, and running it only in the services job would make the fast feedback loop slow. The scripts enumerate paths for real reasons. This makes the enumeration HONEST rather than removing it.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, each specific to a different failure mode, with the mutation verified present before each run per the standing rule. (1) ORPHANED FILE - the exact ai-provider scenario: created packages/core/src/orphan-probe.test.ts named by no script. Output: "1 test file(s) are named by NO npm script, so they run nowhere: - packages/core/src/orphan-probe.test.ts", exit 1. Deleted, verified gone, back to PASS. (2) MISSING FILE - the inverse: appended a nonexistent path to test:unit. Output: "package.json names 1 test file(s) that do not exist", exit 1. A script naming a missing file otherwise fails at run time with a confusing error rather than a clear one. Reverted, verified, back to PASS. IT ALSO REFUSES TO PASS WHILE UNABLE TO LOOK: an explicit assertion requires more than 10 test files to be found, so a broken glob or a wrong root fails loudly instead of reporting "all 0 files registered" - which is precisely the absence-versus-unreadable defect this repository has been bitten by repeatedly. But no pipeline has executed it, and CS-54 just demonstrated that a local green can be actively misleading when the execution environment differs. A CI change verified only by local green is the same class of evidence gap this very ticket is about - things that are not actually executed look identical to things that are. requirements.title: search_jobs and run_events use separate foreign keys where a composite would make a cross-owner row unrepresentable

requirements: Owner isolation is enforced correctly in the application but is not structurally guaranteed by the schema on two tables.
Two tables enforce owner isolation only in the application layer where a composite foreign key, already used elsewhere in this schema, would make a cross-owner row impossible.

evidence: AUDIT FINDING M-1: search_jobs and run_events reference searches.id and users.id SEPARATELY rather than as a composite (owner_id, run_id). lead_history and resume_results already use genuine composite foreign keys, where a cross-owner row is structurally unrepresentable - so the better pattern exists in this same schema and these two tables diverge from it.

NOT A REACHABLE EXPLOIT TODAY, and this is important context: the auditor read every query in v2/apps/api/src/app.ts and confirmed the application layer always scopes correctly. This is defence-in-depth, not an open door. It is also already recorded as an open P2 in .ai/progress.json and remains true.
NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED by the Orchestrator against the schema in this cycle - carried forward as an audit finding. Confirm against v2/packages/core/src before implementing.

MOVED DISCOVERY -> READY 2026-09-25. The only thing holding it in DISCOVERY was its own note that the defect was "NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED against the schema". That was one file read, and it has now been done twice - by the audit and independently in this session. THE DEFECT IS REAL: run_events and search_jobs declare runId and ownerId as SEPARATE SINGLE-COLUMN FKs, while the same file twice uses the composite pattern foreignKey({ columns: [ownerId, leadId] }) and foreignKey({ columns: [ownerId, uploadId] }). The divergence is real, the precedent is established, and nothing about the design is undecided.

UNRECORDED PREREQUISITE FOUND BY THE AUDIT, WHICH WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE SURFACED MID-MIGRATION: a composite FK (owner_id, run_id) -> search_runs(owner_id, id) REQUIRES A UNIQUE CONSTRAINT ON THE REFERENCED COLUMNS. Verified in this session: search_runs does NOT have one. It carries uniqueIndex("search_owner_key").on(ownerId, idempotencyKey) at schema.ts:84 and index("search_owner_created") at :85, and id alone is the primary key.

MEANWHILE BOTH PRECEDENT TABLES CARRY EXACTLY THE HELPER THAT MAKES IT WORK, and they were plainly added for this purpose: uniqueIndex("lead_owner_id").on(ownerId, id) at schema.ts:202 and uniqueIndex("resume_upload_owner_id").on(ownerId, id) at :271. WITHOUT ADDING uniqueIndex("search_owner_id").on(ownerId, id) FIRST, THE MIGRATION FAILS WITH POSTGRES 42830 - no unique constraint matching given keys for the referenced table. That index is the EXPLICIT FIRST MIGRATION STEP.

RECORDED BECAUSE IT GENERALISES: the pattern to copy already existed twice and nobody had noticed the third table lacked its enabler. A migration that follows an established precedent can still fail on the precondition the precedent quietly satisfies.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; re-check if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 17:00 IST on 2026-09-25.

DELIVERED 2026-09-25, and THE ORDERING CONSTRAINT THE AUDIT IDENTIFIED WAS RESPECTED: the search_owner_id unique index landed in 0015_outgoing_pride.sql:1 and schema.ts:90 before any composite FK was added, so Postgres 42830 was never risked. Both target tables converted - composite foreignKey blocks at schema.ts:157 and :178 alongside the two pre-existing ones - and NO single-column references(() => searches.id) form remains anywhere.

TWO MIGRATIONS DELIBERATELY, NOT ONE, and the reasoning is the keeper: 0015 creates the unique index alone; 0016 drops the four single-column constraints and adds the composite FKs. A SEPARATE MIGRATION IS A GUARANTEE; STATEMENT ORDER INSIDE ONE GENERATED FILE IS AN ASSUMPTION.

BOTH WERE GENERATED BY drizzle-kit AND THEN READ - NEVER HAND-WRITTEN. Recorded explicitly because a hand-written migration that happens to work is a different artefact from a generated one that was reviewed.
MIGRATIONS RECONCILE: 17 .sql files, 17 journal entries, verified independently in this session. No orphaned entry, no unjournalled migration.

TYPECHECK IS THE LOAD-BEARING RESULT FOR THIS TICKET SPECIFICALLY, and is cited here rather than only on CS-61: the composite foreign keys changed the SHAPE of run_events and search_jobs, and `tsc -b` exit 0 across the v2 project is what proves NO CONSUMER WAS LEFT REFERENCING THE OLD SINGLE-COLUMN FORM. A migration that applies cleanly but leaves a stale consumer is the failure mode this rules out.

CEILING, WHICH TRAVELS WITH THE NUMBERS: produced on Node v22.23.2 against a declared floor of 24 (.nvmrc, both engines.node fields, ci.yml NODE_VERSION). NONE OF IT IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE SUPPORTED RUNTIME AND NONE OF IT IS CI EVIDENCE - the SHA has not moved.

CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 AFTER CS-76, AND IT NARROWS RATHER THAN RETRACTS THE CLAIM. The load-bearing result cited here is that tsc -b proves no consumer was left referencing the pre-composite single-column form of run_events and search_jobs. THAT REMAINS TRUE FOR SOURCE CONSUMERS. It was never true for TEST consumers: all ten packages/core test files are excluded from the build, so A TEST STILL REFERENCING THE OLD SHAPE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN CAUGHT BY THE TYPECHECK. The runtime suites passing is the evidence covering that gap, not tsc.

BOUNDED TYPECHECK EVIDENCE - RE-WORDED FROM "PROVISIONAL" 2026-09-25, AND THE VERB CHANGE IS THE POINT. This ticket cites a BARE `tsc -b`, which is incremental and was observed exiting 0 while a genuine production error existed (collect.ts TS2353) because a stale .tsbuildinfo declared the project up to date. THAT DOES NOT RETRACT THE RESULT AND DOES NOT MAKE IT SUSPECT: the command ran, it reported truthfully on what it examined, and the source it examined did compile. IT BOUNDS THE RESULT. The run was NARROWER THAN THE CLAIM IT WAS QUOTED FOR - it is evidence that the projects tsc considered up to date had no new errors, not evidence that the tree is clean. "PROVISIONAL" WAS THE WRONG WORD BECAUSE IT IMPLIES THE RESULT MIGHT BE FALSE. It was not false; it was narrow. Re-verify the wider claim with `tsc -b --force` or a cleared .tsbuildinfo - and note that v2 typecheck now begins with --force, so the npm script no longer has this bound. The original lines are deliberately kept: they record what was actually run. NOTHING IS DEMOTED FOR THIS.

requirements.title: Web CSP allows script-src 'unsafe-inline'

requirements: The signed-in web surface permits inline script execution, weakening the main defence against XSS becoming session theft.
The web CSP permits inline scripts. Verified true in source. The API CSP is strict and is not affected.

evidence: VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-25 against current bytes, settling a claim the auditor explicitly could NOT confirm (it had no shell and was carrying it forward rather than asserting it). v2/apps/web/next.config.ts line 27 reads: "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; ". The finding is TRUE.
DO NOT CONFLATE THE TWO SURFACES: the API-side CSP is strict and correct - helmet with default-src 'none' and frame-ancestors 'none'. This finding is about the WEB surface only.

CONTEXT that bounds the severity: docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md already discloses "unsafe-inline styles/scripts remain in CSP" as a residual risk in its threat table, so this is a known, disclosed gap rather than a new discovery. style-src 'unsafe-inline' is substantially harder to remove than script-src and may legitimately remain.

FIXED PROPERLY 2026-09-25 rather than documented-and-accepted, which AC1 also permitted. The blocker was structural: next.config.ts headers() is STATIC, evaluated once at build time, so it cannot emit the per-request value a nonce needs. Added v2/apps/web/src/middleware.ts (there was no middleware in this app before) generating a per-request nonce and setting script-src 'self' 'nonce-<n>' 'strict-dynamic'. The CSP moved out of next.config entirely so there is ONE place a reader must look - two copies of a security policy is how one of them silently drifts. A nonce was chosen over hashes because the App Router emits inline bootstrap and flight-data scripts whose content changes per route and per build; a hash allowlist would need regenerating on every change and would break silently the moment one was missed. 'self' is kept alongside 'strict-dynamic' as the fallback for browsers that do not implement CSP Level 3 - they ignore strict-dynamic and fall back to the host source, still far stronger than 'unsafe-inline'. style-src 'unsafe-inline' is DELIBERATELY RETAINED and recorded as an accepted residual: AC1 is written about script-src, inline styles are a materially smaller risk, and removing them would require nonce-ing every style Next and the component tree emit. Not silently carried - stated in the file and here.

AC3 ("proven by a real browser run, not asserted") SATISFIED. Added an assertion to v2/scripts/check-ui.ts against the REAL DOCUMENT RESPONSE HEADER, not the config file, because the header is what a browser enforces and the config is only one of the places it could come from. IT IS A POSITIVE AND A NEGATIVE ASSERTION ON PURPOSE, and the reason is subtle enough to record: proving a nonce is present would NOT prove 'unsafe-inline' had gone, and a browser IGNORES 'unsafe-inline' whenever a nonce is present - so a policy carrying both would look like it worked while leaving the weaker token in place for any CSP Level 2 browser. The check asserts the directive exists, that it does NOT contain 'unsafe-inline', and that it DOES carry a nonce. VERIFIED: live header on / reads "script-src 'self' 'nonce-YmY3...' 'strict-dynamic'" with no unsafe-inline. Full check-ui suite exit 0 on chromium, firefox and webkit - which is the real proof the app still hydrates, since a nonce mistake breaks every inline script and the suite exercises every route. v2 typecheck 0. VERIFICATION LEVEL: LOCALLY VERIFIED against the dev server. NOT verified against a production build, and NOT CI-EXECUTED.

REVIEWER REJECTED PROMOTION ON AC2 AND WAS EXACTLY RIGHT. AC2 says the strategy must work "with the Next.js App Router in production, not only in development", and my own evidence closed with "LOCALLY VERIFIED against the dev server. NOT verified against a production build." Those two sentences contradicted each other, and the reviewer named the mechanism precisely: statically prerendered HTML is generated at BUILD time and cannot carry a per-request nonce. It asked me to run the production build before anything else. I did, and it broke.

MEASURED FAILURE, NOT INFERRED - this is the durable content of this ticket. npm run build succeeded and listed the middleware as active. Against npm run start:web (a real production server, not the dev server): the response header DID advertise a nonce, but curl on / returned 10 <script> tags and ZERO nonce= attributes. Next did not stamp the nonce onto scripts it had already emitted at build time. Because strict-dynamic makes the nonce authoritative and causes 'self' to be ignored on any browser implementing CSP Level 3, none of those ten scripts could execute. npm run test:ui went RED against production - locator.boundingBox timed out because the page never hydrated. The dev server had passed every one of those assertions minutes earlier. This is precisely the gap AC2 exists to catch, and without the production run I would have shipped a CSP that silently bricks the deployed app.

REVERTED: src/middleware.ts deleted, the policy restored to next.config.ts with script-src unsafe-inline intact, dev server restored, test:ui exit 0 on chromium/firefox/webkit, lint 0, typecheck 0. The full reasoning is recorded in a comment in next.config.ts so the next person does not repeat the attempt blind. WHAT THE REAL FIX COSTS, now known rather than guessed: removing unsafe-inline requires either abandoning static prerendering (forcing dynamic rendering on every route) or moving to build-time hashes of Next own generated inline scripts. Both are genuine architectural decisions with performance and maintenance cost, and neither belongs inside a CSP ticket. This is no longer a header edit. COMPENSATING CONTROLS, verified present: session cookies are httpOnly so script cannot read them; sameSite strict; the API sets its own strict policy (default-src none); no dangerouslySetInnerHTML anywhere in the app; every rendered value goes through React automatic escaping.

F-2 WAS THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING AND IS NOW MOOT BUT WORTH KEEPING: my nonce assertion (assert.match on /'nonce-[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+'/) would have passed happily against a CONSTANT nonce. Hoisting the crypto.randomUUID() line to module scope - a plausible optimisation - would have reduced the policy to an allowlist of one guessable value. A constant nonce is not a degraded CSP, it is a defeated one, and the entire suite would have stayed green. That is a FIFTH check-that-cannot-fail, and the first one caught BEFORE it shipped rather than after. I had implemented the two-request uniqueness assertion before the production run made the whole approach moot. F-3 and F-4 are moot with the middleware gone. F-5 SURVIVES AND WAS KEPT: check-ui.ts now parses the CSP into directives and asserts default-src, object-src, base-uri, frame-ancestors and form-action by EQUALITY rather than substring, so a widened or dropped directive fails. That is real coverage this ticket added and it stays, along with a loud failure when the header is absent entirely. The script-src unsafe-inline weakness is deliberately NOT asserted away - it stays open here.

MEASURED 2026-09-25 (orchestrator session, web tier), and it REVISES THE TICKETS OWN ASSUMPTION. The reverted-nonce comment in next.config.ts concluded that removing unsafe-inline "requires giving up static prerendering OR moving to build-time hashes". Measurement against the real production build shows the first half is unnecessary: ALL 13 app routes are prerendered and ZERO render per request, so every inline script IS known at build time. Static prerendering does NOT have to be abandoned.

THE NUMBERS, from v2/apps/web/.next, confirmed a genuine production build before being trusted (BUILD_ID, prerender-manifest.json, routes-manifest.json and required-server-files.json all present; no .next/static/development directory, so not a dev artefact): 13 prerendered HTML files, 26 inline <script> elements with a body, 0 carrying a nonce (consistent with the earlier measured failure), and only 12 DISTINCT sha256 hashes. One is the (self.__next_f=self.__next_f||[]).push([0]) bootstrap shared by all 13 pages; the rest are per-page Flight payloads. A hash policy needs 12 entries, not hundreds.

WHAT STILL BLOCKS IT IS ORDERING, NOT FEASIBILITY: headers() in next.config.ts is evaluated DURING the build, before the HTML containing those scripts exists, so the hashes cannot be computed and consumed in one pass. Same class of problem as the nonce - a static header trying to describe content it has not seen. Two workable shapes, both needing a BUILD PIPELINE change: a two-pass build (build, hash the emitted HTML, rebuild with headers() reading the generated file), or generating a hash manifest at build time and serving the policy at the edge.

ONE ASSUMPTION EXPLICITLY NOT VERIFIED, stated rather than glossed: the two-pass approach is only viable if the second pass emits BYTE-IDENTICAL HTML. That was not tested, because rebuilding would overwrite .next underneath a dev server running on 5280 that other sessions may be using. Recorded as unverified rather than assumed true.

TWO TRAPS RECORDED BEFORE ANYONE IMPLEMENTS IT. (1) A hash policy that is merely PRESENT proves nothing: asserting script-src contains "sha256-" would pass while unsafe-inline sits beside it - and unsafe-inline is IGNORED once hashes are present, so the policy would look strict, behave strictly, and the assertion would have measured neither. The assertion must be that unsafe-inline is ABSENT, paired with a positive that the page actually rendered. (2) The stale-hash failure is silent in CI and loud in production: if the pipeline forgets to regenerate the manifest the policy still parses and the site still returns 200, with nothing executing.

FAILURE MODE IS A BLANK PAGE, NOT A WEAKER POLICY - the same outcome as the reverted nonce. A single missing hash means React hydration and Flight payloads do not execute. So it must be proven the way the original failure was found: against a PRODUCTION server in a real browser, never against the dev server and never by reading the config.

SCOPE HELD UNDER THE THREE-SESSION PARTITION: the measurement, docs/CSP-STRICT-SCRIPT-SRC.md and the corrected next.config.ts comment are all in the web tier and docs, which this session owns. The IMPLEMENTATION is deliberately NOT started - a two-pass build touches build scripts and the edge option touches infrastructure, both of which belong to the infrastructure session. Handed off rather than half-done. CS-54 stays READY, not promoted; nothing here is CI-executed and the SHA has not moved.

DEMOTED FROM READY 2026-09-25 on independent audit, AND THE TICKET CONTRADICTED ITSELF IN A WAY A PICKER-UP WOULD NOT SEE. Its own final evidence says the implementation is deliberately not started and belongs to the infrastructure session - and it then left itself READY with ownerAgent: Frontend, architectureImpact "Next.js CSP/nonce strategy", no dependency recorded and no owner reassignment. Anyone picking it up as Frontend could not finish it. ownerAgent corrected to Infrastructure in this edit.

THE REMAINING IMPLEMENTATION PATH RESTS ON AN UNTESTED PREMISE, quoted from this ticket: "the two-pass approach is only viable if the second pass emits BYTE-IDENTICAL HTML. That was not tested." That is a DISCOVERY-grade unknown, not a READY task - if the HTML is not byte-identical the hashes are wrong, and the failure mode this ticket states twice is A BLANK PAGE, NOT A WEAKER POLICY. CS-61 needed an amendment; this needs an EXPERIMENT THAT MAY VOID ITS PLAN.

BUT THERE IS A LEGITIMATE SAME-DAY CLOSE NOBODY HAD NAMED, and it comes from reading AC1 cold: it is a DISJUNCTION - "script-src unsafe-inline is removed ... OR retained with a documented, specific reason and a recorded compensating control". BRANCH 2 IS ALREADY SATISFIED AT SOURCE. next.config.ts carries the measured reason (13 prerendered routes, 26 inline scripts, 12 distinct hashes, and the nonce attempts production failure) and enumerates verified compensating controls - httpOnly, sameSite strict, API default-src none, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, React auto-escaping - with the residual already in KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md.

STATUS CHOICE FLAGGED FOR OVERRIDE: the coordinator offered DISCOVERY or close-on-branch-2. This session chose BLOCKED because the deciding input is an OWNER BINARY, and the CS-30 lesson recorded hours earlier is precisely that a ticket waiting on the owner must appear in the BLOCKED column the owner reads - DISCOVERY would hide the cheapest security close on the board in the ideas column. If the coordinator prefers DISCOVERY it is a one-line change.

GENUINE WIN THAT SURVIVED THE REVERT, recorded so the ticket is not read as wholly negative: check-ui.ts now parses the CSP into directives and asserts default-src, object-src, base-uri, frame-ancestors and form-action BY EQUALITY, NOT SUBSTRING. That is permanent coverage this ticket added, independent of whether unsafe-inline is ever removed.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; re-check if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 16:45 IST on 2026-09-25.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. Applies to typecheck, lint, test:unit, deploy:gate:test, eol:check and the three-engine test:ui runs alike.

STALE FIELD CORRECTED 2026-09-25, AND IT WAS THIS SESSIONS OWN: currentStep still opened "READY, reopened" while the status had been BLOCKED for over an hour. That is precisely the field-disagreement defect this session has corrected on CS-38, CS-50, CS-30 and CS-52 today, appearing on a ticket this session had itself demoted. The board renders currentStep, so a reader would have seen READY on a BLOCKED ticket.

THE LESSON IS NOT "BE MORE CAREFUL": it is that changing `status` and changing the fields that DESCRIBE the status are two separate acts, and nothing enforces that the second follows the first. CS-73 already proposes a validator for ownerAgent/architectureImpact consistency; currentStep-versus-status belongs in the same check.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

RE-CONFIRMED BLOCKED 2026-09-26 AND DELIBERATELY NOT ATTEMPTED. Branch 2 of the AC1 disjunction - retain unsafe-inline with a documented reason and a recorded compensating control - IS STILL SATISFIED AT SOURCE: next.config.ts carries "CS-54: script-src unsafe-inline is a real, disclosed weakness and it is STILL HERE - deliberately, with the reason measured rather than assumed", and the middleware history is recorded beside it.

NO WORK WAS ATTEMPTED THIS CYCLE, WHICH IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. The remaining options are (a) close on branch 2, marking AC2 vacuous-and-disclosed, or (b) pursue branch 1, whose only surviving path rests on an UNTESTED byte-identical-HTML premise. BOTH ARE OWNER DECISIONS ABOUT ACCEPTED RISK, NOT ENGINEERING TASKS, so attempting either would be an agent deciding a security posture unilaterally.

AND THE PROHIBITION HOLDS AND IS RESTATED SO IT SURVIVES A FUTURE READER WITH FRESH ENTHUSIASM: DO NOT RETRY THE NONCE MIDDLEWARE. A production run already proved that route ships an application THAT DOES NOT LOAD. That is a stronger disqualification than a failing test, because it was observed against a real build rather than inferred.

2026-09-29 implemented a two-pass production build in v2/apps/web/scripts/build-with-csp.mjs. The first pass discovers 12 inline-script SHA-256 hashes from generated static HTML; a deterministic Next build ID makes the second pass converge and injects those hashes into routes-manifest.json. The shipped policy contains script-src 'self' plus the 12 hashes and no script-src unsafe-inline. A real production next start browser smoke at http://127.0.0.1:5280 rendered the CareerScope workspace shell (not a blank page); the only console errors were expected API-unavailable messages because the local API was not running.

2026-09-29 CI #157 passed all required lanes for cdb81e7 (typecheck/lint/test/build, V2 integration, V2 recovery). Protected Deploy #20 then verified the exact SHA and successfully shipped to production. Live https://careerscope.tech returned HTTP 200 with a hash-based script-src policy containing no unsafe-inline, and /api/health returned {status:ok,version:3.0.0}.

requirements.title: Eleven authenticated GET routes have no rate limit, including the most expensive read, which the UI polls

requirements: A single stuck browser tab becomes a sustained load generator against the most expensive unmetered endpoint in the application.
An existing rate-limit control is applied to two POST routes but not to eleven authenticated GETs, including the most expensive one, which the UI polls every few seconds.

evidence: AUDIT FINDING M-3: eleven authenticated GET routes carry no rate limit. The most significant is GET /api/searches/:id, described as the most expensive read in the application - two 100-row JSONB queries plus a 100-row event scan, with every row re-parsed through Zod.

The client amplifies it: the Jobs page polls /api/searches/:id every 10 seconds while a run is active, and polls /api/searches every 5 seconds UNCONDITIONALLY. So the expensive endpoint is not merely unmetered, it is unmetered and continuously called by the product own UI.

Rate limiting demonstrably EXISTS and works in this codebase - POST /api/account/password and POST /api/account/sessions/revoke-others both carry a real 5/hour limit. So this is an inconsistent application of an existing control, not a missing capability.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED by the Orchestrator in this cycle (route count and polling intervals carried forward from the audit). Confirm against v2/apps/api/src/app.ts and the web query configuration before implementing, and derive the limit from the real intervals.

MEASURED TESTING COST, 2026-09-25 - this finding no longer rests on reasoning alone. While writing the CS-36 cross-session test I used the suite own quiet() helper (waits until no non-streaming request has been in flight for 250ms) on /jobs and it FAILED: "chromium: cs-36 reset /jobs never stopped issuing requests". Cause is exactly this ticket finding: /jobs polls /api/searches every 5 seconds UNCONDITIONALLY, so the route can never reach a settled state. The unmetered polling therefore has a concrete, reproduced cost beyond the hypothetical availability one - it makes a real route structurally untestable by any settle-based technique, and forced the CS-36 test to use a different waiting strategy. That is a second, independent reason to fix it, and it is observable today rather than under load.

HALF THE OUTSTANDING DISCOVERY IS CLOSED 2026-09-25, recorded so whoever picks this up does not redo it. The blocker required confirming against app.ts AND the web query configuration. THE WEB HALF IS CONFIRMED at v2/apps/web/src/components/job-search-view.tsx:70-76 - queryKey ["searches"], enabled: session.data?.authenticated === true, refetchInterval: 5000. An UNCONDITIONAL 5-SECOND POLL OF /api/searches GATED ONLY ON BEING AUTHENTICATED, plus the 10s poll of /api/searches/:id while non-terminal. BOTH NUMBERS MATCH THIS TICKET EXACTLY. Only the app.ts half remains.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; re-check if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 17:00 IST on 2026-09-25.

THE app.ts HALF IS DONE 2026-09-25: eleven routes carry owner-keyed budgets at app.ts:507-831 - searches-read 240/60, leads-read 240/60, profile-read 120/60, market-read 120/60 - with 429 documented in OpenAPI.

THE BUDGET SIZING REASONING IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING, because it is the difference between a limit and a tripwire: the budgets sit ~20x the MEASURED poll rates (12/min and 6/min) ON PURPOSE - "a budget a normal session can reach is one that gets raised the first time it fires". A limit tuned so tightly that ordinary use trips it does not get respected; it gets relaxed, and then it protects nothing.

COMPLETE AS OF 2026-09-25: ALL FOURTEEN AUTHENTICATED GET ROUTES CARRY A BUDGET - eleven newly via readBudget, plus preparation, export and events which already had their own. VERIFIED BY ENUMERATING EVERY ROUTE, NOT BY SAMPLING. That distinction is the one AC1 actually demands, since a sampled inventory cannot establish "authenticated GET routes carry a proportionate limit" of the routes it did not look at.

THE LAST FIX IS THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE: /api/searches/:id/events had its rate limit placed AFTER database.getSearch() and the retained-window query, so AN OVER-BUDGET CALLER STILL COST TWO DATABASE QUERIES PER REJECTION - the limiter was protecting the response but not the resource, which is most of the reason to have one. Moved above both, and deliberately BELOW parsing, so malformed input still receives a deterministic 400 rather than a 429 that hides it.

AC3 IS MET BY A TEST THAT CAN ONLY PASS FOR THE RIGHT REASON, which is materially stronger than a test that passes: with the budget exhausted, a request for a NON-EXISTENT run returns 429 INSTEAD OF 404. That outcome is only possible if the limit precedes the lookup, so the assertion observes the ORDERING rather than merely the limit. FALSIFIED BY RESTORING THE OLD ORDER - 404 !== 429. Both the rejected boundary and its falsification are present.
CEILING, RECORDED SO QA IS NOT READ AS DONE: the evidence is local. The chain to a promotion runs through CI, and that hop has not fired. Promotable on a green CI run; not promoted here.
